findings.issue: The event data and the function's return value are printed as raw memory with the length '_996 - mem[64] + 32': the store at mem[mem[64]] is taken as possibly overwriting mem[64] itself, so mem[64] is re-read and the length does not fold to 32. findings.rule: A store at address p does not change mem[64] when p != 64 is provable; here p is the free-memory pointer, every value stored to mem[64] is >= 128 on all paths (an invariant the analysis can carry), so mem[64] keeps its value, '_x - mem[64]' folds to 0, and the log data / return become address(_128).

notes: All 54 ABI functions (45 defs + 9 consts) and the fallback reviewed; no semantic error found. Same code: the 12 configure / emergencyConfigure functions are one body (diffed: only the admin check, the selector configure 0xf605bf6c / emergencyConfigure 0xb3e035b2, the factory field 0/256/512/768/1024 or _creditFactories, and the event differ, all matching the source); the 6 upgrade*Factory functions are one body (diffed; fields and events match); add/removePeripheryContract share the extractDomain code (fromSmallString scan, indexOf('::'), slice, toSmallString, checked by hand including the empty-slice result 0x60 and TooBigForSmallString). The 9 big functions (shutdownMarket, addToken, shutdownCreditSuite, update* x4, createCreditSuite, createMarket: 800-1800 lines) reviewed by structure: call order, targets, selectors, factory validation (UnauthorizedFactoryException with the right factory in each of the 5 hooks), storage writes, events, returns, forceApprove's three _makeCall branches (return copied to mem[0], extcodesize / returndata == 1 tests) all match. Source loops: _executeHook (inlined ~80 times), _migrateFactoryTargets, the two credit-manager loops, fromSmallString, indexOf's short-search loop and the slice copy are whiles; indexOf's outer 'for {} 1 {}' always breaks and is printed as straight code (counted 'unrolled'); indexOf's long-search loop (searchLength >= 32) is dead for the constant '::' and not counted. P7 = 360 bytes copies left as loops (call data, error strings, event data, ABI decoding of Call.callData); P3 = slice's backward copy with its first word peeled (2); P8 = mem[0]/mem[32] keccak scratch writes; P11 = Panic(50) bounds checks dominated by the loop bound or by SafeMath.sub(len, 1), and pop's Panic(49); P12 = _remove's pop printed in both arms (8 instances).
summary: Faithful on every path checked; the readability problems are the known memory ones: after the first allocation the hook calls lose their targets and arguments (P2, P18), 360 bytes copies stay while loops, and a store at the free-memory pointer hides the return value of updatePriceOracle/updateLossPolicy, while calls with two string arguments print the second one merged into the first.
